recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. The seed request is already satisfied in current core source, and any future eld-19 or eld-20 refinements should be handled through the later, already-audited issue family rather than by changing FHIR-19709 again.
issue_request: FHIR-19709 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction asking to change the ElementDefinition narrative length rule from "Element paths" to "Element names" and to update eld-19 so its expression enforces the stated element-name character and length rules.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites GH#de65b7ad. That merge included commit 7df17c3460e62122489fc1fcd9d13cf270c2c189 (GF#19709), which changed source/elementdefinition.html from "Element paths SHALL NOT exceed 64 characters in length" to "Element names SHALL NOT exceed 64 characters in length" and replaced the old eld-19 path.matches('[^\\s#\\/]+') expression with a fuller character-set and per-component length regex.
additional_context: Later same-family decisions refined the same invariant area without reversing the seed outcome: FHIR-19745 and FHIR-25627 confirmed that the 64-character limit belongs in eld-19; FHIR-19968 corrected eld-19 Schematron/XPath escaping and anchoring concerns; and FHIR-38795 intentionally changed the eld-19 human description to the current component-based wording. Those related issues already have audit commits on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. source/fhir.ini keeps the ElementDefinition page and datatype inputs in build scope; source/elementdefinition.html now states the restriction on element names; and source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml has an anchored eld-19 regex that limits each dot-separated path component to allowed characters and 1-64 characters. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting FHIR-19709 community evidence.
